topic: Braintrust AI Observability Feedback Loops Guide 2026

competitors.title: AI Development Loops — Braintrust Blog (May 2024)
key_points: Defines three core AI development loops: Exploration (quick iteration), Evaluation (systematic testing with scorers), and Data Collection (finding real-world production cases)
Logs, evals, and datasets share the same data structure, making it seamless to flow between loops
Exploration loop uses Playgrounds for rapid prompt/model iteration
Evaluation loop applies scorers across golden datasets for robust testing
Data collection loop starts from production logs, finds patterns, captures inputs, and writes expected outputs

competitors.title: Eval Feedback Loops — Braintrust Blog (Apr 2024)
key_points: Eval = function of (a) data, (b) task/prompts/code, and (c) scoring functions
Three problems solved: finding great eval data, identifying interesting production failures, tying user feedback to evals
Log-to-eval pipeline: trace production runs, find interesting cases, add to datasets, eval, improve, repeat
Scaling via metadata/tag filters, user feedback tracking, and online scores on production traffic
Recommended structure: dataset → Eval(data, task, scores) → results drive improvements

competitors.title: How to Improve Your Golden Datasets with Human Review — Braintrust Blog (May 2026)
key_points: Human review turns production traces into golden datasets with `expected` ground truth values
Topics feature clusters production traces into named categories automatically for routing
Three queue types: triage (decide ignore vs review), SME (fill in ground truth), calibration (cross-reviewer alignment)
Custom trace views embed React components for persona-specific review interfaces
Anti-patterns: leaving expected blank, mixing reference material into expected, deferring review workflow

competitors.title: Why Your Traces and Evals Belong in the Same Place — Braintrust Blog (May 2026)
key_points: Trace-to-eval conversion with one click — suspicious trace becomes dataset entry
Same scorer runs in production and evaluation, ensuring consistency
Automation layer can propose prompt changes, run evals, and surface results without human intervention
Without unified traces+evals, each regression requires a long manual journey through separate tools
Online evals against production traffic catch regressions at the moment they happen

competitors.title: AI Observability: Complete LLM Monitoring Guide [2026] — Techsy (Mar 2026)
key_points: Core pillars: tracing, metrics, evaluation, alerting — with evaluation as observability concern, not just testing
Eval flywheel: observe → evaluate → improve → deploy → observe again — weekly cycles improve quality measurably
LLM-as-a-judge for automated online evaluation scales infinitely and catches majority of quality issues
Agent tracing requires session-level tracing across tool calls, reasoning chains, handoffs, state transitions
8-tool comparison: Langfuse (open-source leader), Braintrust (evaluation-first), Arize Phoenix (ML-focused), Helicone (proxy-based, zero-code), LangSmith (LangChain ecosystem)

stats.fact: AI observability is distinguished from monitoring: monitoring tells you something broke; observability tells you why — critical when failures look identical to successes

angles: Eval-driven development: Treat evaluations as observability, not just testing — run them continuously on production traffic, not just in CI
Unified trace+eval workflow: The single most impactful architectural decision is keeping traces and evals in the same platform to collapse the debug-fix-deploy cycle from days to hours
The eval flywheel: Production failures → new eval cases → better scoring → safer releases → fewer production failures — each cycle makes the system measurably better
Human-in-the-loop feedback: Automated eval scoring catches most issues, but human review with golden datasets and expected values provides ground truth that automated scorers can't replace

Agent-specific feedback loops: As agents get more complex (tool loops, multi-agent, memory, sandboxes), feedback loops must evolve from simple answer scoring to layered trace-span-stage evaluation systems
Cost-aware eval strategy: Budgeted success — 'correct and within budget' — replaces 'correct at any cost' as the headline metric for production AI systems
OpenTelemetry as the foundation: OTEL semantic conventions for GenAI standardize trace structure across tools, making feedback loops portable and future-proof
